title: Crawford Well Depth and Drilling Cost
meta_description: Crawford wells have a 190-foot median depth, with local drilling and complete well costs explained from permit records.
h1: Crawford, Colorado Well Depth, Yield, and Cost
intro_html:
Buying land near Crawford means looking closely at the well, not just the house or acreage. Permit records within 5 miles show 295 wells, with 162 reporting a completed depth. Most are domestic or household wells, and nearly all permits name unnamed or fractured-bedrock aquifers.

The local record points to a generally productive area, but the spread is wide. A typical well is around 190 feet deep, while recorded depths extend much farther. Use these figures to compare a driller’s estimate, question a weak well history, and budget for the complete water system before closing.

sections.heading: Crawford well depths vary with the ground
sections.html:
The median completed well depth near Crawford is 190 feet. The middle half runs from 100 to 262 feet, meaning many local wells fall in that range, but a bid based only on the median would be incomplete. The 90th-percentile depth is 358 feet, and the deepest recorded well reaches 917 feet.

Depth distribution gives useful context: 23% of wells are under 100 feet, 59% are between 100 and 300 feet, 16% are between 300 and 600 feet, and 2% are deeper than 600 feet. Most permits identify unnamed or fractured-bedrock aquifers. In this setting, fractures can make nearby wells behave differently, so neighboring depths help but do not guarantee the result on a new lot.

sections.heading: What Crawford wells produce
sections.html:
Among the 64 wells with a reported pump yield, the median is 14.5 gallons per minute. The middle half runs from 7.0 to 15.0 gallons per minute. Half of the reported wells produce more than 15 gallons per minute, while 33% fall between 5 and 15 gallons per minute.

Low production is present but not dominant: 16% report 1 to 5 gallons per minute and 2% report under 1 gallon per minute. For a buyer, yield is not the same as storage or guaranteed daily supply. Ask for the well construction report, pump test information, and any operating history. A well that makes adequate water slowly may still work for a home if the tank and system are designed around its recovery.

sections.heading: Water levels near Crawford need careful comparison
sections.html:
Only 28 records report a static water level, so the water-level data is much thinner than the depth data. The overall median depth to water is 142 feet, with the middle half from 63 to 214 feet below the surface.

The decade comparison is notable: the median measurement was 182 feet below the surface in the 2010s and 76 feet in the 2020s. That change does not prove a regional rise or fall. It may reflect different locations, seasons, measuring practices, or well types. Do not treat it as a complete groundwater trend. For a property under contract, have the current well measured and compare that result with the original permit and nearby records.

sections.heading: Who has drilled around Crawford, and when
sections.html:
Permit activity is spread across several decades, with the largest period in the 2000s: 143 permits. The records show 18 permits in the 1970s, 13 in the 1980s, 35 in the 1990s, 32 in the 2010s, and 28 in the 2020s. The newest permit year is 2025, so this is not an area with only old well information.

The most active names in these records are Bill Kissner Drilling Inc, also listed as Kissner, Bill F., with 59 wells; Wildcat Drilling & Pump, Inc., also listed as Kissner, Billy D., with 40; and Valley Drilling Co., listed as Stoy, Kenneth, with 23. These records show local experience, but availability, pricing, and current licensing should still be confirmed directly.

sections.heading: Crawford well drilling cost at local depths
sections.html:
For the mixed sedimentary and alluvial ground reported in this area, the drilling model uses $50 to $75 per foot. At the 190-foot median depth, that puts the drilled hole at about $9,500 to $14,200. This is the hole only, not the complete water system.

A finished well with pump, pressure tank, trenching, and electrical is modeled at about $15,500 to $26,200 at that median depth. A 300-foot or deeper hole can push the price higher, especially if casing, grout, access, or difficult formation conditions add work. Get a written bid that separates drilling, casing, grout, pump equipment, testing, trenching, electrical, and any unsuccessful-hole terms.

sections.heading: Crawford risks to check before building
sections.html:
Low yield and dry-hole risk deserve attention because fractured-bedrock wells can change substantially over short distances. The records show 2% of reported yields under 1 gallon per minute, and 16% between 1 and 5 gallons per minute. Those figures are not a prediction for one parcel, but they are a reason to review nearby wells before buying.

There are also 5 PFAS sampling or contamination sites, 1 historic mine-features site, and 1 EPA Superfund or cleanup site mapped within about 10 miles. Check the exact distance and direction from the parcel, then test the well water through a qualified laboratory. Confirm septic setbacks, drainfield space, access for a rig, power routing, and the site’s building envelope. Colorado DWR permit conditions and any augmentation requirements also need review before construction.

faq.q: How deep are wells in Crawford, Colorado?
faq.a: The median completed well depth within 5 miles of Crawford is 190 feet. The middle half runs from 100 to 262 feet. However, 16% of recorded wells are between 300 and 600 feet, and the deepest record is 917 feet. A nearby well is useful evidence, but fractured-bedrock conditions can change the result on a new parcel.

faq.q: How much does it cost to drill a well in Crawford?
faq.a: The local cost model uses $50 to $75 per foot. At the 190-foot median depth, the drilled hole is estimated at $9,500 to $14,200. A finished system with pump, tank, trenching, and electrical is about $15,500 to $26,200. A deeper hole, difficult access, casing, grout, or an unsuccessful hole can change the final price.

faq.q: How much water do wells produce in Crawford?
faq.a: Of the 64 wells with reported pump yields, the median is 14.5 gallons per minute and the middle half is 7.0 to 15.0 gallons per minute. Half report more than 15 gallons per minute. Still, 16% report 1 to 5 gallons per minute and 2% report under 1 gallon per minute, so request the actual well test and recovery history.

faq.q: Is well water safe to drink in Crawford, Colorado?
faq.a: Permit records do not establish that a particular well is safe to drink. Five PFAS sampling or contamination sites are mapped within about 10 miles, along with a historic mine-features site and an EPA Superfund or cleanup site. Test the property’s water through a qualified laboratory, including contaminants relevant to the site, and retest after changes or concerns.

faq.q: Are Crawford well water levels going down?
faq.a: The available water-level record is limited to 28 wells. The median static water level was 182 feet below the surface in the 2010s and 76 feet in the 2020s. That difference alone does not prove a regional trend because locations, seasons, and measurement practices may differ. Have the current well measured and compare it with its construction record.
